title: Servant Freed for a Destroyed Eye or Tooth
kjv_text: And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, that it perish; he shall let him go free for his eye's sake. And if he smite out his manservant's tooth, or his maidservant's tooth; he shall let him go free for his tooth's sake.
summary: A master who destroys a slave's eye or tooth must free the slave — manumission as the damages award, in place of talion.
original_audience: Israelite slaveholders and their slaves, male and female alike.
immediate_context: Immediately after lex talionis: the slave does not get an eye for an eye; the slave gets out. Talion is for the free.
historical_context: Hammurabi 199 pays the *owner* when someone blinds his slave; here, uniquely in the ANE, the compensation goes to the slave, in the currency of freedom. Simultaneously humane (the ANE's only slave-protection of its kind) and stratifying (the slave's eye buys liberty, not equality). The rabbis extended it to twenty-four ruinable body parts.
penalty: Mandatory manumission of the injured slave.
exceptions: None stated; applies to permanent visible maiming, per later interpretation.
nt_passages: Philemon 15-16 — 'not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother' — manumission theology in a letter

internal_contradictions.issue: The slave's eye is worth manumission while the slave's life (if death lingers, v.21) is worth nothing — the code protects the visible injury and shrugs at the fatal one.

usofc_implementation: Codified as the Maiming Manumission Rule in covenant-labor law: certified permanent injury by a bondholder voids the bond with full release. In practice: bondholder-friendly medical examiners, 'pre-existing condition' findings, and a thriving trade in injury documentation. The rule's existence is the OSO's proof the system 'polices itself.'
constitutional_analogue: Workers' compensation crossed with emancipation law; the release remedy has no modern parallel because the underlying bond shouldn't exist.
scene_ideas: A laborer weighing whether a tooth is a fair price for freedom — and the bond-camp dentist who has seen that calculation before.
The medical examiner's two rubber stamps: WORK-RELATED and PRE-EXISTING, and what each costs.
satirical_uses: The regime cites this verse as proof biblical slavery was humane, in pamphlets printed by bonded labor.
